A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LANTERN. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated algorithms and qualitative results.

before.justification: v1 reports original LlamaGen experiments measuring acceleration, acceptance probabilities, image quality and ablation outcomes, with additional qualitative results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Anole results, quality metrics, token-proximity analyses and latency measurements in its appendices.

M1.justification: The neighborhood-based acceptance rule, TVD constraint, rejection resampling and greedy variant remain unchanged between v1 Section 3 and v2 Section 4. Algorithm 1 is retained. The new Algorithm 2 documents precomputation and the previously described incremental neighborhood construction; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The represented coverage remains image-caption generation using LAION-COCO/MS-COCO, ImageNet class-conditioned generation and MT-Bench language diagnostics. Anole adds a model within the retained text-to-image task. Its COCO training split, generated training samples and the replacement qualitative prompts change settings or examples without establishing a distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: The main comparators remain vanilla autoregressive decoding and EAGLE-2. The motivating comparison retains Speculative Decoding, Medusa and EAGLE-2, moving from v1 Table 1 to v2 Figure 2(a). Proximity and divergence ablations retain the same comparison methods. Newly cited Hydra and DistillSpec are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Main timing evaluation changes from 100 captions on an A100 80GB SXM to 1,000 captions on an RTX 3090. Precision, recall and HPS v2 supplement FID and CLIP score. v2 adds Anole training/evaluation settings and matched-acceptance TVD/JSD configurations. LlamaGen's reported top-p changes from 0 in v1 Appendix C to 1.0 in v2 Appendix B.2; this establishes a reporting change, not proof that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative token-replacement sensitivity, visual-versus-language neighbor comparisons, caption-count sensitivity, component and divergence-metric latency analyses, spatial neighborhood-size analysis and additional quality-metric trade-offs (Appendices C and F–H). Table 3 improves the TVD/JSD ablation by comparing matched accepted lengths. The original drafter-target distribution heatmap is removed; the original appendix image grids are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Although v2 calls its caption-count and token-replacement analyses statistical, they report point estimates across experimental settings rather than introducing uncertainty estimation or a new statistical estimator.

E6.justification: Existing main-table FID, CLIP scores and accepted lengths are retained, while timing values change under revised conditions; for example, sampling at delta=0.4 changes from 1.65x to 1.69x. v2 adds precision/recall/HPS v2 results and Table 6 reports LANTERN speed-ups of 1.64x on Stage II and 1.17x on Anole, versus EAGLE-2's 0.96x and 0.73x. Numerous proximity, latency and ablation results are newly reported.

T1.justification: The acceptance equations, distorted distribution, TVD constraint and neighborhood construction retain their mathematical substance. v2's preliminaries explain standard autoregressive factorization, codebook mappings and notation. No substantive new assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The quantified headline acceleration claims are updated: the abstract's sampling advantage over EAGLE-2 changes from 1.76x to 1.82x, with corresponding introduction updates. The central claims about token-selection ambiguity, LANTERN's novelty and acceleration with limited quality loss remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of preserved precision versus reduced diversity, declining preference scores, and the limits of unconstrained token interchangeability at large neighborhoods. It also explains spatial neighborhood-size patterns through higher uncertainty at image-row starts and attributes additional latency to proximity-set computation. The detailed v1 explanation of limited greedy acceleration at small k is replaced with more general trade-off discussion.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands documentation through motivating-experiment drafter architectures and sample counts, Anole training and generation settings, explicit neighbor-precomputation pseudocode, component timing information and the qualitative prompt list (Appendices B, D, F and I). Most existing LlamaGen training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Conversely, the acceptance-probability table loses its earlier description of averaging over 100 image generations.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of Anole, CogView, Parti, DistillSpec and Hydra, alongside references supporting the new metrics. It removes Gagrani et al. and the explicit distinction from multimodal speculative decoding that generates text. These broaden and adjust contextual comparisons while retaining the paper's central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 introduces a full preliminaries section, consolidates and rewrites the token-ambiguity discussion, revises results and trade-off explanations, and substantially rewrites related work. Original algorithm, implementation and qualitative appendices move from B/C/D to D/B/J within a reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: The original baseline table becomes Figure 2(a), and Figure 2 is redesigned with different diagnostic panels. Figures 1, 3 and 4 use replacement examples; Figure 4 has fewer rows. The main results table gains grouped quality-metric columns, and new analysis tables, token-patch visualizations, heatmaps and pseudocode are added. Original appendix Figures 6–11 survive as Figures 8–13.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the mechanism and speed-quality trade-off. Quantitative replacement tests expose limits previously supported mainly by examples; precision/recall and HPS v2 reveal additional quality costs; Anole evaluation and matched-acceptance ablations strengthen validation. Expanded implementation details improve reproducibility. Local latency inconsistencies remain: Appendix F.2 quotes 24x/7x ratios for delta=0.4, whereas Table 8 implies approximately 32x/9x. These localized problems do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
